welcome.label: Welcome

blocks.prompt: What's bringing you to the course?

blocks.body:
This isn't a test – there are no right or wrong answers. We ask these questions now, and again at the end, simply to help you see how far you've travelled through the course.

To what extent would you agree with the following statements?

blocks.prompt: I have a detailed understanding of what the Bible teaches about 'work' and 'calling'
I have a detailed understanding of what my God-given talents/gifts and limitations are
I have a strong sense of what God's specific 'call' and purpose is for my life
I have a clear, practical plan for how to pursue God's purpose for my life, in terms of 'work' / 'calling'
I am at peace with God's plan for my life

clauses.message: Choose what's bringing you to the course to continue.

sections.title: How you've been designed – your strengths

next_step.heading: Start with your gifts.
next_step.sentence: Start with the ten-minute strengths evaluation.

blocks.label: The big question
blocks.body: Based on what people you trust say about you, and your own self-examination, what gifts and talents has God given (and not given) you? Remember – you don't have 'church gifts' and 'non-church gifts'. A teaching gift looks different in a school vs in kids' work, but it's still a teaching gift.

blocks.heading: Scripture on gifts

passages.text: Having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us, let us use them: if prophecy, in proportion to our faith; if service, in our serving; the one who teaches, in his teaching; the one who exhorts, in his exhortation; the one who contributes, in generosity; the one who leads, with zeal; the one who does acts of mercy, with cheerfulness.

For to one is given through the Spirit the utterance of wisdom, and to another the utterance of knowledge according to the same Spirit, to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by the one Spirit, to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another the ability to distinguish between spirits, to another various kinds of tongues, to another the interpretation of tongues.

And God has appointed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing, helping, administrating, and various kinds of tongues. Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles? Do all possess gifts of healing? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret?

Show hospitality to one another without grumbling. As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace: whoever speaks, as one who speaks oracles of God; whoever serves, as one who serves by the strength that God supplies—in order that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ. To him belong glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.

blocks.note: As you read, reflect: what gifts do you see in yourself? Which do others affirm in you? Which are notably absent – and what might that tell you about how God has designed you?

blocks.label: Your activity
blocks.body: This section uses the strengths evaluation, where you sort short statements about your strengths into buckets, which takes about 7 minutes. You can also invite people you trust to do the same for you.
Sort your strengths into buckets, fine-tune the intensity of each – then invite at least 3 trusted people to evaluate you too.

finished.body: You've completed the strengths evaluation. You can review your results any time.

clauses.message: Complete the strengths evaluation to continue.

coach_brief.title: Session 1 – Their gifts
coach_brief.purpose: Help them believe what the strengths evaluation is telling them, and notice where they discount themselves.

questions.text: Which of these results surprised you, and which felt obvious?
Where others rated you higher than you rated yourself – why do you think that gap is there?
What is something you are good at that you have stopped noticing because it comes easily?
Which of these strengths do you actually enjoy using, and which just drain you?

watch_for.text: People routinely dismiss their strongest gift as "nothing special". If they wave something away, slow down and ask about it.
A low score is not a failing. Help them read the whole profile, not just hunt for weaknesses.

coach_brief.avoid: Do not treat the strengths evaluation as a verdict. It is a conversation starter, not a diagnosis.

blocks.body:
Workbook 1, to work through on paper: two readings on how you've been designed, then a conversation with your coach about your results, your own answers and the answers others gave.

It is the first of four for the middle of the course, one for each of Sections 2 to 5. When you've finished this one, come back here to say so.

after_comparison.message: This opens once you've seen how others see you. That needs at least 3 of the people you invited to answer.

blocks.body:
Workbook 2, to work through on paper: mapping your story, and what has happened in each season of it.

When you've finished it, come back here to say so.

You will need a pen, a Bible, and somewhere you’re unlikely to be interrupted. Your ‘gifts and talents’ results may not be fully complete, as it can take a while to get others to provide their evaluations of you – don’t let that stop you making progress on your journey.

clauses.message: Opens once your coach has accepted. If they decline, choose someone else.

opens_when.with_sections: Opens once you've {sections}, and your coach has accepted.

blocks.body:
Workbook 3, to work through on paper: narrowing your calling to a sentence, then opening it back up.

When you've finished it, come back here to say so, and Section 5 opens.

Workbook 4, to work through on paper: turning all of it into something you will actually do.

When you've finished it, come back here to say so, and Section 6, a letter to your future self, opens.

sections.title: A letter to your future self

blocks.label: The task
blocks.body: Write to yourself as you will be on the day you choose for your letter to open, between three months and two years from now. You have just done a lot of thinking, and most of it fades faster than you would expect. Put it down now, while it is still warm. When you finish this section, your letter is sealed until that day, and then it opens here for you to read.

passages.text: “When your children ask in time to come, ‘What do those stones mean to you?’ then you shall tell them that the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD. When it passed over the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. So these stones shall be to the people of Israel a memorial for ever.”

blocks.note: When Israel crossed the Jordan, God told them to carry twelve stones out of the riverbed and pile them on the bank – so that when their children asked “what do these stones mean?”, they would have something solid to point at. Memory needs help. This letter is your pile of stones.

side_card.lead: A coach helps you test what you're discovering with someone who knows you and your faith.
side_card.sentence: You'll need one before the later sections open.

blocks.heading: Walking with a coach
blocks.lead: This choice matters more than any other you'll make in the course.
blocks.body:
The work ahead asks you to be honest about your gifts, your disappointments and what you actually want from your life. That only goes somewhere useful if the person walking alongside you is the right one.

The wrong choice usually isn't a bad person. It's someone who can't resist solving it for you, or who knows you too little to notice when you're avoiding something, or who won't have the time when it matters.
blocks.not_needed: Someone who tells you what they'd do in your position, or who has a view on where you should end up.
blocks.needed: Someone who asks the questions in the material, listens hard, and lets you reach your own conclusions.
blocks.footnote: We say coach rather than mentor deliberately. A mentor passes on their own experience. A coach draws out yours — which is the harder job, and the one this needs.
blocks.name_prompt: Who are you thinking of asking?
blocks.name_hint: Just a first name for now. Six quick questions follow — answer them honestly rather than generously.
blocks.coach_invitation:
They're working through Whatever You Do, a course on discerning vocational calling. It asks some searching questions, and it works far better with someone alongside.

Before you say yes, read what's actually being asked. It's a real commitment, and saying no now is much better than fading out halfway.
blocks.coach_accepted: You've agreed to all six. That's the contract, and it's worth returning to if a conversation starts drifting into advice.
blocks.coach_declined:
Saying no now is far better than agreeing and fading out halfway. {name} will simply be told you weren't able to, with no detail.

If it's only the time commitment, it's worth telling them directly — they may be able to work around it. If it's that you'd struggle to ask rather than advise, that's genuinely useful for them to know, and there's no shame in it. Most people would.

blocks.label: Who knows you best?
blocks.body:
One of the most valuable parts of this course is comparing how you see yourself with how others experience you. We often miss things about ourselves that others can see clearly.

We need at least 3 people whose opinion you trust – people who know you well enough to be honest. They'll receive a short survey about your strengths, through a link you send them.

observers.privacy_notice:
[Draft: this notice must be written properly before anyone real takes part.]

{name} has asked you to help them see their strengths as others see them. You'll sort some strengths into buckets and adjust the intensity of each. Takes about 10–15 minutes.

What we keep: your answers. You don't give your name: we know who this link was sent to because {name} added you to their list. {name} never sees which answers are whose, though the people who run the service can.

What {name} sees of your answers: nothing until enough people have answered. Then, the average of everyone's answers, and each person's answers without their name, lowest first, as a word such as "Strong" and a dot on a line. {name} may also choose to show this to a trusted third party. Your name is never shown with your answers. Once {name} has looked at the combined results, no new answers are added.

If you change your mind, you can withdraw at any time, and your answers will be removed: through the link of your own you're shown when you start, even after it has expired, or by asking the people who run the service. If you haven't answered, we'll email you a reminder once a week until your link runs out, and every reminder lets you stop them. This link is yours alone, so you answer only once and can stop the reminders or withdraw. {name} sees your answers among everyone else's, never with your name on them.

presentation.disclaimer: Important: This is a free, rapid, directional tool, designed to give you a useful starting point for reflection and conversation. It is not backed by extensive psychometric datasets or rigorous validation (yet). Please treat these results as indicative, not definitive.

generalist.heading: You’re a generalist
generalist.text: Both your profiles are flat: every result reads Present or Strong, with none leading and none less used. That’s a real result rather than an error: you draw on all of these in much the same measure. Better to say so than force a winner.
generalist.after_pairs: Both your profiles are flat, even after your answers to “Which is more true of you?”: every result reads Present or Strong, with none leading and none less used. balanced.level: {names} came out level after your answers to “Which is more true of you?”. That’s a real result rather than an error: they sit equally in you.

skipped.heading: Skipped

gaps.heading: 🔍 Biggest Gaps
gaps.intro: Where your self-perception differs most from how others experience you. These are the most fruitful areas for reflection and conversation.

others_higher.label: Others rate higher
others_higher.description: Others see this as more of a strength in you than you do yourself. This could be a hidden strength – something that comes so naturally you don’t recognise it as special.

you_higher.label: You rate higher
you_higher.description: You rate yourself higher here than others do. This could mean you value this more than it’s currently visible to others, or that your self-image in this area is stronger than your current expression of it.

gaps.modest: A modest gap – worth noting but not necessarily significant.

comparison.prompts_intro: These are designed for honest reflection – ideally with a coach or trusted friend.

prompts.title: Hidden strengths
prompts.text: Where others rate you higher than you rate yourself – what might it mean that you undervalue these? Could you lean into them more intentionally?

prompts.title: Blind spots
prompts.text: Where you rate yourself higher than others do – is this an area where your intention doesn’t yet match your impact? Or do others simply not see this side of you?

prompts.title: Confirmed strengths
prompts.text: Where you and others agree – these are your most reliable strengths. How are you stewarding them?

prompts.title: The surprise
prompts.text: Which gap surprised you most? What would change if you took that feedback seriously?
